incident-bot: :rotating_light: HOSTED-RUNTIME ALERT: OOMs observed on kv-cache shard cluster-7. High memory growth correlated with long prompt sessions and continuous-batching windows. Error rate spike + SLO violations.
Amber (oncall): I'm on it. Paging Raj and Maria. Any immediate customer-facing symptoms?
Jamie (support): Getting chat failures reported from customer 'BrightLedger' and a few smaller customers — timeouts + 500s. CS has a handful of screenshots.
Liz (CS): Confirmed — BrightLedger saw multiple failed completions since ~00:42 UTC. They're seeing partial responses then timeout. Flagging as P1 for them.
Raj SRE: Observing kv cache live metric: active_kv_entries per-request skyrocketed. Continuous batching windows appear to be growing with repeated long-context requests (>= 80k tokens). Prefetch queue backlog increased x40.
Maria (runtime): That matches traces — long prompts keep pinning KV pages and we don't evict fast enough because prefetch keeps re-populating. Memory climbs until OOM.
Amber (oncall): Short-term mitigation ideas? Can we throttle prefetch or reduce batch window?
Raj SRE: We can flip the prefetch flag at runtime for hosted pool to conservative. Also reduce max_batch_window from 1024 to 256 for affected pool.
Maria (runtime): I can push a hotpatch to runtime config to disable aggressive prefetch for the hosted pool and force strict LRU eviction. Patch ready, needs infra approval to apply to cluster-7.
Tina (ops): I'll run the change via canary first (cluster-7-a -> 10% traffic). Command I plan to run:

```
infractl rollout start --cluster cluster-7 --target 10% \
  --set runtime.kv.prefetch.enabled=false \
  --set runtime.kv.eviction_policy=lru \
  --set runtime.kv.max_batch_window=256
```

Tina (ops): ETA 3m to start canary.
Amber (oncall): Good. Jamie/Liz, please notify affected customers about temporary degradation and that we're applying mitigations.
Jamie (support): On it. Messaging draft to BrightLedger: "We're aware of elevated failures for long-context sessions; applying mitigations that may temporarily affect throughput but should restore stability." Will send and paste copy here when done.
Ryan (devex): I'll run a quick query to identify offending tenant ids and recent request token lengths:

```
SELECT tenant_id, max(tokens), count(*) FROM request_logs
WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY max(tokens) DESC LIMIT 20;
```

Ryan (devex): Found ~6 tenants with repeated requests >60k tokens, top one is tenant_87 (BrightLedger).
Raj SRE: Recommend also applying a per-tenant max_context=64k soft cap with 429 + guidance page while we stabilize. Lower-impact than full throttling.
Maria (runtime): Agree. I can enable the soft cap at infra layer for hosted with ramp: 64k soft cap, 96k hard cap that drops to 64k on repeated requests. Config snippet:

```
runtime.kv.context_limits:
  soft_limit_tokens: 65536
  hard_limit_tokens: 98304
  repeated_violation_window: 5m
```

Amber (oncall): Tina, include that in the rollout? We want prefetch off first, then soft caps.
Tina (ops): Canary started, 10% traffic diverted, logs look stable so far. No immediate OOMs on canary nodes. Rolling to 50% now.
Jamie (support): Sent BrightLedger update: they acknowledged and are reducing bulk debug prompts. Asking for ETA to full fix.
Liz (CS): Keeping them on a bridge until we confirm full recovery; asked for any recommended prompt length limits.
Raj SRE: I'm seeing memory growth rate drop on canary after prefetch flag disabled. Heartbeat metrics show reclaimed pages.
Maria (runtime): Initiating soft cap toggle now via runtime control plane. Command:

```
runtimectl set-context-limits --soft 65536 --hard 98304 --apply-hosted=true
```

Maria (runtime): Applied to hosted pool. Monitoring.
Ryan (devex): Running an automated sweep to tag recent requests > soft limit and route telemetry to the incident channel.
Ryan (devex): Sweep found spike at 00:41 UTC — correlated with scheduled large-batch experiment from internal customer test — possible root cause amplification.
Amber (oncall): Note that for postmortem. For now: prefetch disabled + LRU eviction + soft caps applied. Any remaining customer 500s?
Jamie (support): Errors dropping significantly — BrightLedger reports back that retries are passing and no new failures in the last 6 minutes.
Liz (CS): They're happy for now but want a writeup. I'll gather timeline + next steps.
Tina (ops): Rolling to 100% completed at 00:58 UTC. No further OOMs observed on cluster-7. Monitoring for 30m.
Raj SRE: Opening a blocked ticket to disable internal experiment that caused high-length requests and adding guardrails. Also schedule a quota for internal test tenants.
Maria (runtime): We'll follow up with a runtime patch to make prefetch adaptive: do not prefetch for sequences > 32k and cap per-request prefetch budget. I'll draft PR.
Amber (oncall): Handing off to Raj for overnight monitoring and postmortem. Raj, taking the secondary?
Raj SRE: Acknowledge. I'll take handoff at 01:10 UTC. Action items: 1) Confirm no regressions in the 30m window, 2) collect telemetry (top offending tenants and stack traces), 3) coordinate PR with runtime team.
Amber (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving channel.
Raj SRE: Noted. I'll prepare initial incident summary and severity assessment. Early severity: P1 for BrightLedger (customer-visible), P2 platform-wide potential.
Liz (CS): I'll send BrightLedger the incident summary draft after you review.
Ryan (devex): Putting a dashboard link for the follow-up: https://dash.rewrd/kv/cluster-7?range=1h
Tina (ops): Ops note: patch rollback plan ready if memory flares on other clusters.
Maria (runtime): PR link for adaptive prefetch: https://git.rewrd/runtime/pull/4028 — will iterate.
Raj SRE: Handoff complete. Last check-in 01:20 UTC shows stable. Will produce postmortem within SLA window.
Jamie (support): Closing the immediate CS bridge, will reopen if BrightLedger reports further issues.
incident-bot: Incident channel will remain open; please tag updates with #postmortem when available.
